name: Squallline Null

stars.name: Squallline
stars.notes: Flare-active red dwarf prone to sudden X-ray squalls that wash the inner system without warning, giving the system its name.

planets.name: Cinderwake
planets.notes: Airless rock scoured by centuries of flares; its regolith is laced with exposed iron and cobalt veins.

planets.name: Parch
planets.notes: Tidally locked dune world whose narrow terminator ring hosts automated solvent-mining rigs working subsurface brines.

planets.name: Graybow
planets.notes: Compact methane giant ringed by permanent electrical squalls; drone tankers skim deuterium from its calm polar caps.

planets.name: Rimfrost
planets.notes: Frozen volatile reservoir tapped for water, shielding ice, and bulk oxidizer feedstock.

anomalies.name: The Saltfire Maelstrom
anomalies.notes: A recurring plasma vortex that feeds on stellar flares; miners time belt operations to its erratic cycle, and Consortium models still fail to predict it.

asteroid_belts.name: The Gravel Squall
asteroid_belts.notes: High-grade ferrous and platinum-group ore in dense clusters; autonomous cutter swarms work the richest strands on rotating schedules timed to flare lulls.

stations.name: Harrow Point
stations.notes: Fully robotic processing head bolted to a nickel-iron core; human supervisors dock only during rare extended quiet periods.

faction_control.notes: A single corporate extraction license covers the whole system. Pirates rarely brave the flare cycle, and the Consortium's drones handle what little security is needed.

history: Surveyed during the second-wave mineral rush by a Giltwater Consortium long-range probe that barely survived a direct flare strike.
A flare surge destroyed the original crewed camp in the belt; operations were rebuilt from scratch as fully automated.
Consortium ledgers show steadily rising yields as predictive models of the star's flare cycle grow more accurate.
description: Squallline Null is a tight four-world system circling a temperamental red dwarf whose frequent flares wash the inner planets in X-ray fire. Between the third and fourth orbits churns the Gravel Squall, a dense metallic belt glittering with exposed platinum-group ores. Near the star itself, heat shimmer and charged particles bend sensor returns into rolling waves, like wind over hot steel.

Everything of consequence here belongs to the Giltwater Consortium, whose robotic cutters strip the belt while drone tankers sip deuterium from Graybow's calmer latitudes. No humans live aboard Harrow Point; crews visit in short shifts timed between flare events. Traffic is limited to scheduled ore barges making the long haul back to the Mistral Frontier.

Rumor holds that the star's squall cycle has been slowly intensifying, and that Giltwater's models cannot yet say why. Independent prospectors occasionally sneak in during quiet stretches, gambling against the star's temper. Some claim the Gravel Squall's dust lanes shift in patterns that mirror the flare schedule—a coincidence no one has explained.
